items.title: Threat Hunting Using Memory Leaks in Banner Grabs
items.description: A stray string in STUN banner data turned out to be leaked stack memory from a previously unknown coturn 4.10.0 vulnerability (CVE-2026-104074), and the shape of the leak reveals how each server was built.

items.title: Easy File Uploader for Joomla: It's Right There in the Name
items.description: VulnCheck's Initial Access Intelligence team details CVE-2026-107904, an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload in the Easy File Uploader module for Joomla, where an extension blacklist and a finfo MIME check both fall to a GIF89a polyglot named .phtml, landing a webshell in the web root of any install that maps .phtml to PHP.

items.title: AI Has Changed VulnCheck
items.description: VulnCheck's Initial Access team started as two people producing 3-5 n-day exploits and detection artifacts per week, but now delivers hundreds, driving an explosion in Canary network observations, faster coverage, and more first-to-market exploits than ever before.

items.title: Attackers Exploit CVEs to Harvest Credentials
items.description: Credential-harvesting attempts appeared across 127 of 694 CVEs observed in VulnCheck Canaries (18%), with monthly records rising roughly sixfold from July to October.

items.title: What This Year’s Recognition Signals About How Security Teams Are Changing
items.description: Vulnerability exploitation is the top cause of breaches. What VulnCheck’s 2026 recognition says about exploit intelligence and where to start.

items.title: Java4Shell CVE-2026-114938: Fine, I Guess We’ll Do This Again
items.description: A critical vulnerability in OpenJDK could allow for code execution on specific hardware if ASLR can be bypassed

items.title: One Recovery Code, Two Shells in Control Web Panel
items.description: VulnCheck's Initial Access Intelligence team discloses two vulnerabilities in Control Web Panel that both end in code execution as the hosting account from the same primitive, an account password-recovery code. One poisons the reset link's Host header to leak the code, and the other feeds that code to the administration API, which accepts it as OAuth authorization.

items.title: Identifying FortiGate Firmware From a Single ClientHello
items.description: About 376,000 internet-facing FortiGate hosts expose their FGFM management port and answer a connection with a TLS ClientHello. A JA4 fingerprint of that ClientHello places each host in a FortiOS generation, which maps to a range of versions and the CVEs that affect them. 160,171 hosts (42.6%) are in generations where every version we measured has a known-exploited CVE.

items.title: Exploitation Flows Targeting Japan
items.description: Last week, we traveled to Tokyo, Japan, to present at the Machina Cyber Intelligence Summit. For the talk, we dug into our VulnCheck Canary detections to see what regional exploitation activity looks like across the Canaries we host in Japan.

items.title: Code of the Day: Unauthenticated Root in Copeland XWEB EVO
items.description: VulnCheck's Initial Access Intelligence team discloses 14 vulnerabilities in the Dixell / Copeland XWEB EVO refrigeration supervisor, including unauthenticated remote root on both the legacy builds and the current end-of-support firmware, where the login handler runs the submitted username as a shell command before the password check, the interpreter behind every page is setuid root, and the daily admin credential is a secret-free function of the device MAC and the date.

items.title: After 7-months, Glasswing Overwelms Maintainers with Underwhelming Findings
items.description: Seven months into Project Glasswing, VulnCheck has tracked 442 CVEs attributable to Anthropic, roughly 0.5% of all CVEs published this year, with only two identified as exploited in the wild. Of Anthropic’s 37,966 reported findings, only 7,349 (19.4%) have been made public and just 217 have been marked fixed.

items.title: Same Attacker, Different Door: Our Canaries Caught Microsoft's Agentic AI Secret Hunter Exploiting Langflow
items.description: On November 5, Microsoft Threat Intelligence published research on threat actors using agentic AI tooling to hunt for secrets exposed on GitHub. With those secrets they got into Entra ID tenants, Azure Key Vaults and Azure AI services.

items.title: CWP2Shell: The Login Page That Never Says No
items.description: VulnCheck's Initial Access Intelligence team details an unauthenticated pre-auth remote root RCE chain in Control Web Panel, where the user panel emits its login redirect without stopping execution, so an attacker-named module file runs before authentication and a root-owned user API turns that foothold into uid 0.

items.title: Exploitation Targeting Node-RED, a Tool Embedded in ICS Products
items.description: On October 30, 2026, one of our canaries caught an attacker exploiting CVE-2026-58115, an unauthenticated Node-RED admin API flaw, to deploy a flow that downloads and runs a Linux bot. The request came from an IP in Microsoft's ASN (AS8075).

items.title: VulnCheck Opens Initial Access Community Edition to the Public
items.description: VulnCheck releases free, open community edition of initial access exploits and detections.

items.title: Cache Me If You Can: Unpacking a Go Implant and Its Toolkit
items.description: An investigation into Gotenberg CVE-2026-42589 exploitation in VulnCheck Canary Intelligence led us to cache_base, a custom Go reverse shell, and a much larger multi-platform toolkit.

items.title: What a Canary Sees That a KEV Entry Can't
items.description: 1,981,869 exploitation events from VulnCheck canaries show who attacked, what they ran, and where they called home. That's the evidence a KEV entry can't give you.

items.title: Exploring the Risks and Impacts of AI on Vulnerability Discovery and Exploitation
items.description: We take a look at how AI makes the capabilities behind each one more accessible and accelerates how quickly attackers can use them.

items.title: PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
items.description: Two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, allow for unauthenticated remote code execution.

items.title: SPIP odt2spip Plugin: Authenticated Command Injection via Uploaded Document Filename
items.description: VulnCheck's Initial Access Intelligence team details an authenticated OS command injection in the SPIP odt2spip plugin, where an uploaded document's filename is concatenated into a shell command and run, giving any low-privileged author remote code execution as the web server user.
